A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VarEOT work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-to-Swiss-roll simulations and image-translation experiments, including FID/LPIPS results in Table 2 and supplementary analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds VarEOT results on MSCI single-cell data and a training-time/particle-count study. Table 2 distinguishes original VarEOT results from borrowed baseline results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 corrects the reported Langevin drift: v1 scales only the quadratic-cost gradient by 1/epsilon, whereas v2 scales the potential gradient as well, matching Equation (5). The accompanying inference density is corrected accordingly. The variational training objective and joint two-network procedure remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: New Section 5.2 adds biological single-cell distribution interpolation on MSCI, covering four donors and trajectories from days 2 to 4 and 3 to 7 with intermediate-day evaluation. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained synthetic example and face-translation tasks.

E2.justification: The new MSCI comparison includes Sinkhorn (Cuturi, 2013), Minimax (Gushchin et al., 2023) and IPF (Vargas et al., 2021), alongside the Langevin-based EgNOT comparator. These additional methods have reported comparison results, explicitly borrowed from Korotin et al. (2024). The original image comparisons retain LightSB and EgNOT.

E3.justification: The MSCI experiment introduces intermediate-distribution evaluation using energy distance, PCA dimensions 50/100/1000 and K=128. Appendix C.1 adds a timing protocol with 10,000 training iterations and K values from 32 to 512, using GPU execution for VarEOT/EgNOT and CPU execution for LightSB. Existing image splits, metrics and inference budgets are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.1 and Table 4 examine how particle count K affects training time and FID, adding a focused computational sensitivity analysis. The existing epsilon-diversity and Langevin step-size/step-count analyses remain in Figures 6–7.

E5.justification: New Table 2 reports MSCI results averaged over two setups and five random seeds, with 95% confidence intervals. v1 provides no corresponding empirical uncertainty reporting. This is reporting for the added benchmark, not evidence of increased repetitions for the retained image experiments.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports VarEOT energy distances of 2.45, 2.31 and 1.47 for PCA dimensions 50, 100 and 1000. Table 4 adds timing/FID results, including 85 seconds/13.45 at K=32 and 409 seconds/9.575 at K=512. These are added results under their stated settings. All numerical scores in v1 Table 2, now v2 Table 3, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces dimension-dependent Lipschitz-class rates with O(N^(-1/2)+M^(-1/2)+K^(-1/2)) under bounded, clipped neural-network classes. Proposition 3.4 now analyzes the joint empirical maximizer. Appendix A substantially revises contraction arguments, explicitly accounts for finite-K Gaussian sampling error, and replaces the approximation proof with a neural-network construction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding impact discussion retain the same central contributions: exact variational reformulation, simulation-free neural training, learning guarantees and competitive translation. Changing 'positive normalizer' to 'log-normalizer' aligns terminology with the existing formulation. The added experiments support the retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds substantive limitations concerning auxiliary-network expressiveness and restriction to quadratic costs. The new experimental discussion interprets the particle-count speed–quality trade-off and attributes the advantage over EgNOT to avoiding training-time simulation. Existing inference-sampling and numerical-instability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a VarEOT code-repository link and discloses clipping exponential arguments above 30 and gradients at norm 1. It also documents MSCI particle count/hardware and hardware allocation for timing comparisons. These are additional reproducibility disclosures; the PDFs do not establish that clipping was newly introduced. Some MSCI settings remain deferred to cited external work.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting literature on single-cell transport, energy distance, neural-network complexity and approximation, including Bunne et al., Koshizuka and Sato, Golowich et al., Maurer and Pinkus. Gottlieb et al. and Ledoux–Talagrand are removed with the replaced proof arguments. The central positioning against existing EOT/SB approaches is retained.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the learning-guarantee narrative, joint optimization and the distinction between simulation-free training and inference. Grammar and terminology are corrected, front matter is updated, acknowledgements are added, and experimental subsections are inserted and renumbered. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the MSCI and timing tables and relocates existing displays as the text expands. The original image-results table becomes Table 3 and corrects the A→Y label to A→C. Figures 1–7 retain their experimental content, with appendix figures redistributed across pages and minor caption edits.

improvement.justification: The rewritten learning analysis addresses v1's mismatch between its theoretical estimator and jointly trained networks, includes previously omitted finite-K sampling error, and supplies an explicit neural-network approximation argument (Section 3.3 and Appendix A). Together with corrected inference scaling and the new biological and timing experiments, this substantially strengthens theoretical and empirical support. Hardware differences in timing comparisons and externally deferred MSCI settings still limit interpretation and reproducibility.
